points.title: 早年教育
points.description: 加尔文出生于法国北部努瓦永的一个中产阶级家庭，父亲是主教座堂的财务主管。他接受了当时最好的教育，先在努瓦永学习拉丁语，后在巴黎学习人文学科和神学。1528年，遵从父亲意愿，他前往奥尔良学习法律，展现出非凡的学术才能。这一时期，他接触到了人文主义思想，并开始对宗教改革产生兴趣。1532年，他出版了自己的第一本书《塞内卡论仁慈》，展示了他作为古典学者的才华。
points.descriptionEn: Calvin was born in Noyon, France, to a middle-class family; his father was an administrator in the local cathedral. He received an excellent education, first studying Latin in Noyon, then humanities and theology in Paris. Following his father's wishes, he studied law in Orleans from 1528, demonstrating exceptional academic abilities. During this period, he was exposed to humanist ideas and began developing an interest in the Reformation. In 1532, he published his first book, 'Commentary on Seneca's On Clemency,' showcasing his talent as a classical scholar.

points.title: 宗教改革觉醒
points.description: 1533年，加尔文经历了宗教皈依，从人文主义者转变为新教徒。次年，因参与新教活动被迫离开巴黎，前往昂热、巴黎和奥尔良等地。1535年，他前往巴塞尔，开始系统性地阐述自己的神学思想。1536年，他出版了《基督教要义》的第一版，这部著作后来成为新教改革的核心神学著作。同年，在前往斯特拉斯堡的途中，因战争被迫停留在日内瓦，这成为他人生的重要转折点。
points.descriptionEn: In 1533, Calvin experienced a religious conversion, transforming from a humanist to a Protestant. The following year, he was forced to leave Paris due to his Protestant activities, traveling to Angers, Paris, and Orleans. In 1535, he went to Basel and began systematically articulating his theological ideas. In 1536, he published the first edition of 'Institutes of the Christian Religion,' which later became a core theological work of the Protestant Reformation. That same year, on his way to Strasbourg, he was detained in Geneva due to war, marking a major turning point in his life.

points.title: 首次改革尝试
points.description: 1536年，加尔文抵达日内瓦，迅速与法勒尔等人合作，推动宗教改革。他起草了《日内瓦信仰告白》和《教会纪律》，试图建立一个基于新教原则的教会秩序。然而，他的严格改革措施引起了部分市民的反对。1538年，市政当局拒绝批准他的教会法令，加尔文与法勒尔被迫离开日内瓦，前往斯特拉斯堡。在斯特拉斯堡，他担任法国难民教堂的牧师，并完成了《基督教要义》的修订版，同时深入研究圣经注释。
points.descriptionEn: Arriving in Geneva in 1536, Calvin quickly collaborated with Farel and others to promote the Reformation. He drafted the 'Confession of Faith of Geneva' and 'Ecclesiastical Ordinances,' attempting to establish a church order based on Protestant principles. However, his strict reform measures provoked opposition from some citizens. In 1538, the city authorities refused to approve his ecclesiastical ordinances, and Calvin and Farel were forced to leave Geneva for Strasbourg. In Strasbourg, he served as pastor of a French refugee church, revised the 'Institutes of the Christian Religion,' and engaged in extensive biblical studies.

points.title: 流亡与成长
points.description: 在斯特拉斯堡的三年间，加尔文担任法国难民教堂的牧师，积累了宝贵的教会管理经验。他完成了《基督教要义》的重大修订，扩展了这部神学巨著的内容。同时，他开始系统性地撰写圣经注释，特别是对保罗书信的注释。在这期间，他与改革家布塞尔的密切合作，进一步深化了他的改革思想。1541年，日内瓦局势变化，新当选的市政当局邀请加尔文返回日内瓦，这标志着他人生新阶段的开始。
points.descriptionEn: During his three years in Strasbourg, Calvin served as pastor of a French refugee church, gaining valuable experience in church administration. He made a major revision of the 'Institutes of the Christian Religion,' expanding this theological masterpiece. He also began systematically writing biblical commentaries, particularly on Paul's epistles. During this period, his close collaboration with reformer Bucer further deepened his reform ideas. In 1541, the political situation in Geneva changed, and the newly elected city authorities invited Calvin to return, marking the beginning of a new phase in his life.

points.title: 改革领袖
points.description: 1541年，加尔文返回日内瓦，开始了长达二十多年的改革领导生涯。他建立了完整的教会体系，包括四个牧师和十二位长老组成的宗教会议，以及教会纪律法庭。他推行严格的社会道德规范，禁止赌博、跳舞和戏剧等娱乐活动。在教育方面，他创办了日内瓦学院（后来的日内瓦大学），培养了大量改革人才。1555年后，加尔文在日内瓦的权力达到顶峰，被称为'日内瓦教皇'。在此期间，他完成了《基督教要义》的最终版本，并撰写了大量圣经注释，对后世新教神学产生了深远影响。1564年，加尔文在日内瓦逝世，享年54岁。
points.descriptionEn: Returning to Geneva in 1541, Calvin began his over twenty-year career as a reform leader. He established a complete church system, including a consistory of four pastors and twelve elders, and ecclesiastical courts. He enforced strict social moral codes, banning gambling, dancing, and theatrical performances. In education, he founded the Geneva Academy (later the University of Geneva), training numerous reform-minded individuals. After 1555, Calvin's power in Geneva reached its peak, earning him the title 'Pope of Geneva.' During this period, he completed the final version of the 'Institutes of the Christian Religion' and wrote numerous biblical commentaries, profoundly influencing later Protestant theology. Calvin died in Geneva in 1564 at the age of 54.

supporter.zh: 加尔文被视为宗教改革最重要的神学家之一，他的神学思想为新教奠定了坚实的理论基础。支持者赞扬他强调上帝的主权、圣经的权威和信徒的呼召，这些思想深刻影响了基督教的发展。他建立的日内瓦模式成为新教教会的典范，影响了后来的长老会、公理会等教会传统。加尔文主义强调纪律、秩序和勤奋，对西方资本主义精神的形成产生了重要影响。他的圣经注释和神学著作至今仍是新教神学研究的重要资源。
supporter.en: Calvin is regarded as one of the most important theologians of the Reformation, whose theological ideas provided a solid foundation for Protestantism. Supporters praise his emphasis on God's sovereignty, the authority of Scripture, and the calling of believers, which profoundly influenced Christian development. The Geneva model he established became a paradigm for Protestant churches, influencing later Presbyterian, Congregationalist, and other church traditions. Calvinism's emphasis on discipline, order, and diligence significantly contributed to the formation of the Western capitalist spirit. His biblical commentaries and theological works remain essential resources in Protestant theological studies.

critic.zh: 批评者指责加尔文在日内瓦实行神权统治，压制个人自由和思想多样性。他们特别批评他对待异见者的态度，包括对塞尔维特处以火刑的决定。批评者认为加尔文建立的宗教法庭过于严苛，干涉市民的私人生活。他的神学思想被批评为过于宿命论，导致消极的人生态度。此外，加尔文对艺术和娱乐的限制也被视为对人性压抑的表现。这些批评者认为，加尔文虽然对宗教改革有贡献，但其统治方式和神学思想存在严重缺陷。
critic.en: Critics accuse Calvin of implementing theocratic rule in Geneva, suppressing personal freedom and intellectual diversity. They particularly criticize his treatment of dissenters, including his decision to burn Servetus at the stake. Critics argue that the ecclesiastical courts he established were overly harsh and interfered in citizens' private lives. His theological ideas are criticized as excessively deterministic, leading to消极 attitudes toward life. Additionally, Calvin's restrictions on art and entertainment are seen as suppressing human nature. These critics believe that while Calvin contributed to the Reformation, his methods of rule and theological ideas had serious flaws.

objective.zh: 历史学界普遍认为，加尔文是宗教改革的关键人物，其影响远超日内瓦的范围。他的神学思想形成了加尔宗这一重要的新教传统，影响了全球数百万信徒。在流行文化中，加尔文常被简化为严苛的道德主义者，但历史研究表明，他的思想更为复杂。他既强调上帝的主权，也重视人的责任；既坚持严格的教义，也鼓励学术研究。加尔文对现代民主制度、资本主义伦理和西方教育体系的发展都有深远影响。他的遗产是复杂的，既有促进宗教宽容和思想进步的一面，也有导致宗教冲突和压制异见的一面。
objective.en: Historiography generally regards Calvin as a pivotal figure of the Reformation whose influence extended far beyond Geneva. His theological ideas formed the Calvinist tradition, one of the major Protestant branches influencing millions of believers worldwide. In popular culture, Calvin is often simplified as a stern moralist, but historical research shows his thought was more complex. He emphasized both God's sovereignty and human responsibility; maintained strict doctrine while encouraging academic study. Calvin profoundly influenced the development of modern democratic institutions, capitalist ethics, and Western education systems. His legacy is complex, containing both aspects that promoted religious tolerance and intellectual progress, and those that led to religious conflict and suppression of dissent.

self.zh: 我们不是为今生而活，而是为永恒而活。
self.en: We are not here to live for ourselves, but for eternity.

others.zh: 加尔文是所有改革家中最伟大的，因为他建立了最完善的体系。
others.en: Calvin was the greatest of all the reformers because he established the most perfect system.
